description: Approves new storm sewer construction on 46th Street East.
Mitigates flooding near 46th Street East and 1st Avenue North.

chips.text: Residents and businesses near 46th Street East and 1st Avenue North.

description: Saskatoon applies for Carthy Foundation funding.
Partners with University of Saskatchewan for green infrastructure research.

chips.text: Partnership with Global Institute for Water Security.
Funding supports urban green infrastructure research.

description: Funds $4.7 million Material Recovery Centre expansion.
Exempts Household Hazardous Waste Facility from net-zero energy policy.

chips.text: Delegate noted no site map or operating budget provided for hazardous waste facility.
Delegate suggested returning to weekend collection for hazardous waste to increase volume.

speakers.name: Sherry Tarasoff
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: MRC Expansion - CHIF Project Approval
said: Expressed concern over lack of detailed cost breakdowns for projects.
City-run hazardous waste program is less effective than contractor-run.
Questioned status of mattress recycling funds and organic facility construction.

description: Recommends new transit bylaw, requiring kenneled animals.
Amends public spitting and appeal board bylaws.

chips.text: Bus drivers face increased responsibility for unaccompanied children and dealing with incidents.
Councillor Dubois believed administration would review age limits across facilities
How will fines be collected from homeless individuals?
Mary Fedun reported daily unsafe situations, intoxication, and fare evasion on buses.
Sporadic enforcement risks charges of harassment and discrimination against certain groups.
Need for free tickets for citizens in least fortunate circumstances.
Administration will include app issue solutions in public communications and FAQs.

speakers.name: Robert Clipperton
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: New Transit Bylaw
said: Commends bylaw for addressing disorder; supports education and suspensions.
Questions specific rules: "threats to comfort," sleeping, and child age requirements.
Highlights implementation challenges and calls for public engagement and fare review.

speakers.name: Mary Fedun
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: New Transit Bylaw
said: Commends council for bylaw, ensuring consistency with city services.
Concerned about lack of enforcement, public intoxication, and driver safety.
Suggests distributing rules and regulations, like the library did.

description: Saskatoon will apply for federal funding for Riversdale streetscaping.
If successful, $1.5 million will fund Capital Project P.02162.

chips.text: Residents of the Riversdale neighbourhood are affected.
Project aims to grow community canopies, improving local environment.

description: Approves scope change for golf course driving ranges project.
Increases project budget by $1,615,000 to $3,015,000.
Funding comes from the Golf Course Capital Reserve.

chips.text: Saskatoon golf course patrons will benefit from project changes.

description: Saskatoon provides fixed-term loan to TCU Place.
Loan funds new theatre sound system installation.
City borrows $3,800,000 from its investment portfolio.
Funds will acquire 2950 Lorne Avenue for a Municipal Works Yard.
City to create interim parking lot at 52 - 25th Street E.
Cost is $150,000 from Capital Project P.01420.
A third-party operator will manage the revenue-generating lot.
City buys 1,959 sq ft from St. Thomas More College for $158,700.
City buys 7,133 sq ft from St. Andrew's College for $690,000.
Land acquired for future transportation infrastructure.
Updates City Council Policy C03-036 on multi-year budget planning.
Amends Bylaw No. 9170 on board communications.
Funds community safety services for Avenue C and public washroom.
Restores regular commissioner patrols in the Avenue C area.
Funding approved through December 31, 2026.

chips.text: Increased demand at Avenue C women's drop-in center and public washroom highlights vulnerability.

speakers.name: Randy Pshebylo
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Community Safety Update
said: Riversdale BID is excluded from community safety plan committees.
Businesses are leaving due to safety issues and financial losses.
Quicker response times and better enforcement of laws are needed.

description: Appoints Natalie Cargan to Board of Revision until end of 2026.
Appoints Emily Gabor to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Advisory Committee.
She represents Greater Saskatoon Catholic Schools until 2028.
Mayor Block, Councillor Davies, Councillor Ford appointed to advisory group.
Appoints Councillor MacDonald to Meewasin Valley Authority until end of 2026.
Ellen Hunks appointed to Municipal Planning Commission until 2028.
City will readvertise for Saskatoon Appeals Board vacancies.
Recommends new development incentives for established neighbourhoods.
Offers reduced tax abatements for larger housing projects.
Replaces two existing housing incentive policies.

chips.text: Councillor Parker argued incentives without zoning tools are poor messaging.
Developers of market housing in established neighbourhoods.
Delegate Patrick Wolfe supported tax abatements for infill development in older neighbourhoods.
Concerns raised that market housing incentives could reduce affordable housing focus.
City will explore long-term tax exemptions for affordable, supportive, transitional housing.

speakers.name: Patrick Wolfe
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Proposed New Development Incentives Policy
said: Infill development is costly and faces many barriers.
Saskatoon lags other Western cities in infill development.
Tax abatements are essential for building rental apartments in older areas.

description: Acquires land at 1130 and 1030 Idylwyld Drive North.
Purchases land from Saskatchewan government for $1.00.
Saskatoon would explore a strategic partnership with Muskeg Lake Cree Nation.

chips.text: City Manager stated an EOI would be disingenuous, likely leading to the same partner.
This direct negotiation approach for a project of this scale may set a new precedent.
The identity of other nations who approached the city for partnership was not disclosed.
One speaker expressed public distrust and concern over limiting the bidding process for the project.

speakers.name: Chief Kelly Wolfe
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: DEED - Indigenous Partnership Opportunity
said: Opportunity to build on 38-year relationship with Saskatoon.
Urban reserve has 700+ employees, medical center, university campus.
Partnership could bring professional hockey, jobs, tourism, federal capital.

speakers.name: Jason Aebig
said: Welcomes partnership; MLCN pioneered first urban reserve with city.
Economic study: district could inject $1.37 billion locally.
Delay means higher costs and lost major event opportunities.

speakers.name: Cary Tarasoff
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: DEED - Indigenous Partnership Opportunity
said: City's TIF plan is broken; honesty required before proceeding.
Mayor excluded advisory groups; asks about other interested entities.
Questions federal lobbyist Doug Richardson's involvement.

speakers.name: Randy Pshebylo
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: DEED - Indigenous Partnership Opportunity
said: Downtown and Riversdale are connected; success benefits both districts.
Appreciates business mindset and proven track records of First Nations.
Supportive of continuing dialogue to find answers to questions.

speakers.name: Stephanie Pocha
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: DEED - Indigenous Partnership Opportunity
said: Saskatoon's visitor economy reached nearly $900 million last year.
Supports partnership with MLCN and leadership of STC chiefs.
Infrastructure alone doesn't create success; demand generation does.

description: Extends 210 Pacific Avenue emergency shelter use for 8 months.
Lease and tax exemption for 210 Pacific Avenue also extended.
This allows completion of new 31st Street purpose-built shelter.

chips.text: Staff clarified the city has limited control over the new shelter's construction timeline.
Taxpayers will cover approximately $14,000 annually for the tax exemption.
Residents near 210 Pacific Avenue reported positive experiences with the shelter.

description: Increases Shaw Centre score clock funding by $187,000.
Funded from Leisure Services Equipment Replacement Reserve.
Authorizes early servicing for Holmwood high school site, before concept plan approval.
East Side Leisure Centre project proceeds with original scope, $95 million budget.
City explores YMCA partnership for operations.
Leisure Centre exempt from Net Zero energy policy.

chips.text: Councillor Jeffries questioned administration's previous confidence in budget estimates.
East side's six neighborhoods, 80,000 residents, will use the facility.
Council asked for cost-benefit analysis of adding two more swim lanes.
Community wants accessible, inclusive, and welcoming aquatic and fitness spaces.
YMCA offers subsidized memberships; one in five participants receive assistance.
Administration committed to report on improving capital project cost estimate communication.

speakers.name: DeeAnn Mercier
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: East Side Leisure Centre
said: YMCA builds healthy, connected communities, ensuring access and inclusion.
Partnership offers financial sustainability through diverse funding and membership.
Proven model with city ownership, YMCA operations, and community focus.

description: The 2026 edition of the City of Saskatoon Municipal Manual was presented.
Amends Capital Reserve Bylaw 1993.
Renames waste container replacement reserve.
Becomes waste utility capital reserve.
Proposes five-year property tax exemption for Saskatoon Soccer Inc.
Applies to Kinzman Hague Brew and Saskatoon Soccer Centres.
Exemption would run from 2026 through 2030.
